MI Farooqui with Ruhul Quddus and Abdul Mannan Kha, Advocates ------ For the Petitioner. 
Abdul Kader Talukder; Assistant Attorney-General with Nahid Mahtab, Assistant Attorney-General ------ For Respondent No.2.
parties:
Hanif Shaikh (Md) ------ Petitioner
Vs.
 Government of Bangladesh and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
SAN Mominur Rahman J: Rule was issued as to why the office order bearing No. Memo No. Je: Pro: Nat: //8-4/02/423 dated 4-7-2002 passed by the respondent No. 2 cancelling the declaration of "Dainik Uttarbanga Barta" evidenced by Annexure E to the writ petition, should not be declared to be without lawful authority and of no legal effect. 

 4. Mr Md Ruhul Quddus, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner, submits that the respondent No. 2 has manifestly exercised his jurisdiction not invested in him under section 20 of the said Act in cancelling the declaration of the newspaper by the. impugned order communicated vide Memo No. Je: Nat:/8-4/02/423 dated 4-7-2002, evidenced by Annexure 'F' in the writ petition. The learned Advocate referring to section 20 of the said Act submitted that the cancellation of any declaration subsequent to authentication of any newspaper can only be made (a) if a proprietor, the printer or the publisher of the newspaper ceased to be a citizen of Bangladesh; (b) if the printer or the publisher has been convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude or under President's Order 8/72; or (c) that if the printer or publisher has been found to be a lunatic or of unsound mind by a Court of law and (d) if a publisher ceased to have financial resource required for regularly publishing the newspaper, but in the instant case neither in the show cause notices any of such allegation has been made nor there was any occasion to attract any of the said four (4) criteria of section 20 of the said Act. It has been submitted that if there be any false news published in the newspaper action may be taken under section 31 of the Act apart from application of provisions of the Penal Code and that for non-supplying of copy of the newspapers as required by section 26 of the Act, action is to be taken under the provisions of section 35 of the said Act, which provides maximum fine of Taka 500 for every default. Learned Advocate lastly, submitted that the action of the respondent No.2 in cancelling the declaration of the newspaper is without any lawful authority and violated the right of the petitioner .guaranteed by Articles 31 and 39 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

 5. Mr Abdul Kader Talukder, Assistant Attorney-General with Ms Naheed Mahtab, Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the respondent No.2, submitted that admittedly the names of the Hon'ble President, Hon'ble Prime Minister and Leader of the Opposition has been published incorrectly in the newspaper on 26-3- 2002 which has created confusion in the mind of the public and the newspaper issue in reference being the Independence Day issue, the writ petitioner ought to have been more cautious in the printing of such news and the same cannot be condoned on the basis of the corrigendum published in the newspaper as claimed. Learned Assistant Attorney- General however, found it difficult to show us that the allegations as made in the show cause notices and the impugned order of cancellation, evidenced by Annexure AI dated 27-3-2002, Annexure C dated 24-6-2002 and Annexure E dated 7-2-2002 respectively to the writ petition, attract any of the criteria mentioned in section 20 of the said Act. 

 6. We have considered the statements made in the writ petition as well as the submissions made by the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner and those of the learned Assistant Attorney-General, we are of the view that the impugned order of cancellation vide Memo No. Je: Pro: Nat/8-4/02/423 dated 4-7-2002, evidenced by Annexure E to the writ petition, has been passed without lawful authority inasmuch as the allegation as made in the show cause notice evidenced by Annexure AI can at best attract section 31 of the Act, that too if such publication is found to be malafide. But in the instant case, the authority regretted the mistake occurred in the news item published on 26-3-2002 in the next two issues of the newspaper on the first page published on 28th and 29th March, 2002 as corrigendum and we do not find any malafide in the mistake referred to above occurred in the issue of the newspaper published on 26-3-2002. Further, it appears that in the second show cause notice (Annexure C) a fresh allegation of non-compliance of section 26 of the Act has been made, which also has been denied in the reply. The addition of new allegation in the second show cause notice is bad in the eye of law. In the order of cancellation (Annexure E) it further appears that another new allegation as to non-publication of newspaper regularly. which was absent in the second show cause notice. has been alleged and that no opportunity has been given for reply to such new allegation and thus the impugned order of cancellation is ex facie bad. Considering the requirements of section 20 of the Act. we are of the view that no provision of section 20 is attracted to any of the allegations made in the show cause notices or in the impugned order of cancellation of the declaration and thus. the impugned order of cancellation of declaration of the newspaper appears to be not bonafide, and has been issued without lawful authority. 

 In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost. The order of cancellation of the declaration of the Dainik Uttarbanga Barta vide Memo No. Je: Pro: Nat/8-4/02/423 dated 4-7-2002, evidenced by Annexure E to the writ petition, is hereby declared to have been passed and issued without lawful authority and of no legal effect.
